edges.description: Secreted alpha-toxin acts on host-cell membranes, initiating the membrane-injury step of myonecrosis.
edges.source: Anaerobic clostridial toxin production in infected muscle

edges.description: Alpha-toxin membrane injury, together with theta-toxin, drives the vascular leukostasis that follows.
Absorbed alpha-toxin entering the circulation produces systemic shock and erythrocyte lysis.
Endothelial injury and capillary leak from leukostasis produce the marked localized edema of gas gangrene.
Reduced arteriolar flow and anoxia from vascular leukostasis drive progressive necrosis of large muscle groups.
Ischemic muscle injury produces the severe pain out of proportion to external findings characteristic of clostridial myonecrosis.
Toxins reaching the arterial circulation precipitate systemic shock and multiorgan failure.
Alpha-toxin lysis of erythrocyte membranes produces massive intravascular hemolysis and hemolytic anemia.

nodes.description: Alpha-toxin and perfringolysin O act together to produce vascular leukostasis; toxin-damaged endothelium, platelet aggregation, leukocyte trapping, capillary leak, and impaired oxygen delivery create a self-amplifying anaerobic and necrotic muscle compartment.

evidence.reference_title: Use of genetically manipulated strains of Clostridium perfringens reveals that both alpha-toxin and theta-toxin are required for vascular leukostasis to occur in experimental gas gangrene.
evidence.snippet: Thus, both alpha-toxin and theta-toxin are necessary for the characteristic vascular leukostasis observed in clostridial myonecrosis.

Toxin-induced endothelial dysfunction and microvascular injury could also cause loss of albumin, electrolytes, and water into the interstitial space resulting in marked localized edema. These events, combined with intravascular platelet aggregation and leukostasis, would increase venous pressures and favor further loss of fluid and protein in the distal capillary bed.

nodes.description: C. perfringens alpha-toxin is a phospholipase C/sphingomyelinase that binds target-cell membranes through its C-terminal domain and triggers membrane lipid turnover, endocytosis, and cell death.

evidence.reference_title: Membrane-Binding Mechanism of Clostridium perfringens Alpha-Toxin.
evidence.snippet: Alpha-toxin possesses phospholipase C and sphingomyelinase activities. The toxin is composed of an N-terminal domain (1-250 aa, N-domain), which is the catalytic site, and a C-terminal domain (251-370 aa, C-domain), which is the membrane-binding site.

evidence.reference_title: Virulence studies on chromosomal alpha-toxin and theta-toxin mutants constructed by allelic exchange provide genetic evidence for the essential role of alpha-toxin in Clostridium perfringens-mediated gas gangrene.
evidence.snippet: The results showed that the plc mutants had demonstrably reduced virulence and therefore provided definitive genetic evidence for the essential role of alpha-toxin in gas gangrene or clostridial myonecrosis.

nodes.description: In devitalized or otherwise permissive soft tissue, anaerobic C. perfringens proliferates and elaborates extracellular toxins and enzymes that initiate rapid skeletal-muscle necrosis.

evidence.reference_title: Virulence studies on chromosomal alpha-toxin and theta-toxin mutants constructed by allelic exchange provide genetic evidence for the essential role of alpha-toxin in Clostridium perfringens-mediated gas gangrene.
evidence.snippet: The pathogenesis of clostridial myonecrosis, or gas gangrene, involves the growth of the anaerobic bacterium Clostridium perfringens in the infected tissues and the elaboration of numerous extracellular toxins and enzymes.

nodes.description: Progressive local edema follows toxin-induced vascular leak in clostridial myonecrosis.

evidence.snippet: Similarly, the direct cytotoxicity of PFO could disrupt endothelial integrity and contribute to progressive edema both locally and systemically.

nodes.description: Massive intravascular hemolysis can complicate severe C. perfringens sepsis.

evidence.reference_title: Clostridium Perfringens Infection in a Febrile Patient with Severe Hemolytic Anemia.
evidence.snippet: While C. perfringens sepsis is uncommon, it is often rapidly fatal because the alpha toxin of this bacterium induces massive intravascular hemolysis by disrupting red blood cell membranes.

nodes.description: Coagulative necrosis of skeletal muscle is the defining lesion of clostridial myonecrosis and the feature the disease is named for.

evidence.reference_title: Membrane-Binding Mechanism of Clostridium perfringens Alpha-Toxin.
evidence.snippet: Clostridium perfringens alpha-toxin is a key mediator of gas gangrene, which is a life-threatening infection that manifests as fever, pain, edema, myonecrosis, and gas production.
